rationale: Two narratives the BSB renders as forced ('by force', 34:2; 'he violated her', 2 Samuel 13:14), the second about Tamar, whose protests 13:12-13 records, share a cluster of Hebrew words. Bible Hub's interlinear shows: the verb 'innah (Strong's 6031, Piel) at Genesis 34:2 (BSB 'lay with her by force') and at 2 Samuel 13:12 and 13:14 (BSB 'Do not humiliate me'; 'he violated her'); the noun nebalah (5039) at 34:7 (BSB 'an outrage') and 13:12 (BSB 'this disgraceful thing'); and the clause 'such [a thing] is not done' (ken lo ye'aseh) with 'in Israel' (beyisrael) at 34:7 and 13:12 (BSB 'a thing that should not be done' and 'such a thing should never be done in Israel'). Named readers pair the stories: Rachel Adelman (Jewish Women's Archive) lists 2 Samuel 13:12 among the 'outrage' parallels and contrasts Shechem with Amnon; Shawna Dolansky and Alison Joseph (TheTorah.com) set 2 Samuel 13:12-14 beside 34:2 in their arguments about 'innah; Amy-Jill Levine (L'Osservatore Romano, 2024) writes that 'Stories of rape and revenge repeat'; Keil and Delitzsch on 34:31 compare the brothers' revenge with Absalom's (in the same note they cite nineteenth-century Arab punishment of 'seduction' by death, a comparison this row does not take up). Graded motif at strong, following conn-gen30-build-gen16 (shared Hebrew wording, published readers pair the passages), not allusion: 2 Samuel 13 names neither Dinah nor Shechem, and no source read argues that one text depends on the other. The readers above use the comparison to opposite ends in the dispute over 'innah reported in the lesson's Position 1; this row does not settle that dispute.
